assumptions: The owner can define a paid repair or maintenance package that is meaningfully different from an unplanned walk-in repair.
The owner can complete the reserved appointments within five delivery hours.
Customers can book and pay through the shop's existing arrangements without new software or cash expenditure.
proposals.proposal: Repair the bicycles of opted-in customers through a paid, pre-booked service offer emailed only to those forty customers; the owner shares the offer and reserves a limited number of service-counter appointments. Use EUR 0 additional cash and up to six hours: one hour to define the offer and email it, and five hours to deliver up to the reserved appointments. Measure replies, bookings and completed paid services; continue only if at least three customers book and the work fits the six-hour cap, otherwise stop.
proposals.reason: The ordered components support a paid service offer, targeted contact and bounded delivery. The proposal uses existing tools and the counter, no software, hiring or advertising, and no recurring spend. It is distinct from ordinary walk-in repair through advance booking and a limited service allocation, although the exact paid service and prices remain to be set. Demand is not assumed: bookings and completed payments provide the signal.

assumptions: The owner may devote and schedule all six hours for the inspection pilot.
A paid inspection is sufficiently distinct from ordinary walk-in repair for existing customers.
The existing counter can support limited inspection appointments without disrupting ordinary operations.
Customers will accept the proposed price and booking process.
proposals.proposal: Allocate the six hours, share a paid limited-time inspection offer with the forty opted-in customers, and use the existing repair tools to deliver booked bicycle inspections. Email preparation and contact would use about one hour, with up to five hours for inspections. Charge a set price, record bookings and completed payments, and continue only if at least three customers purchase; otherwise stop after two weeks.
proposals.reason: The proposal can fit the supplied time, cash and resource limits and uses the permitted email audience. A paid inspection can be distinct from ordinary walk-in repair, and the booking/payment threshold gives an observable decision rule. However, the component meaning is somewhat strained: 'lend' does not clearly establish how the owner provides the six hours, and the candidate does not specify the bounded appointment arrangement as clearly as required. The inspection proposition, price and customer willingness remain assumptions.

assumptions: Customer contact would occur only by email to the forty opted-in customers.
The repairs would be offered as a separately priced, limited pilot rather than ordinary walk-in work.
The shop has enough unallocated capacity within six additional hours.
proposals.proposal: Count the existing repair tools, repair the forty existing customers, then share the service counter. A possible completion would use an email invitation to opted-in customers for a limited counter-based paid repair service, but the seed only establishes ordinary repair activity and does not establish a distinct proposition, price, capacity, or measurement rule.
proposals.reason: This is operationally more coherent than the other seeds and could use existing tools and the counter without new software, hires, or advertising. However, repairing customers is not clearly a service proposition beyond ordinary walk-in repair, and the sequence supplies no staff-time or cash accounting, bounded appointment arrangement, paid-demand signal, or continue-or-stop rule. Contact-channel compliance depends on the proposed email completion rather than the supplied components.

assumptions: The owner can define a useful paid assessment distinct from ordinary repair.
The owner can set a pilot price and reserve a limited appointment pool within six additional staff hours.
Only the forty opted-in customers are contacted through the existing email channel.
Preparation, email handling, booking, delivery and measurement together remain within six staff hours.
Any cash expenditure remains at or below EUR 120 with no recurring commitment.
A pre-set paid-booking or conversion threshold is established before launch.
proposals.proposal: Measure customer-reported bicycle condition through a paid, bounded assessment; restore engagement with the existing opted-in customer relationship by sending one service email; and pool a limited set of assessment appointments at the existing counter. Charge for the assessment, track paid bookings and completed appointments, and continue only if a pre-set number or conversion rate is reached. The seed gives the proposal a coherent measurement, relationship and pooled-exchange sequence; pricing, message content and exact appointment cap are supporting proposals.
proposals.reason: This is the strongest complete proposal in the batch. It tests a distinct paid assessment service rather than ordinary walk-in repair and can fit the limits if the email preparation and sending, booking administration, assessments and recording are capped at six hours and incidental costs at EUR 120. It uses only the existing tools, counter and opted-in customers. The proposal still assumes customers will agree to pay and that the owner can deliver the pooled appointments within the stated capacity; those are unmeasured rather than established facts.

assumptions: The owner can define and reserve a limited health-check service using existing tools.
The owner can email all forty opted-in customers through the existing channel without new software or advertising.
The owner sets prices, a paid-booking threshold and appointment durations that keep total work within six hours and cash within EUR 120.

proposals.proposal: Restore the existing customer relationship by emailing the forty opted-in customers a paid bicycle health-check service, pool the owner's six available hours into a small set of reserved appointments, and cap the number of bookings and total delivery effort during the two-week pilot.
proposals.reason: This sequence supports a distinct paid service beyond ordinary walk-in repair and can fit the limits if the owner uses the existing email channel and tools, spends no more than EUR 120, and caps preparation, customer contact and appointments within six total staff hours. The observable demand signal is paid bookings or deposits from the emailed customers; continue only if the defined minimum number of paid bookings is reached, otherwise stop. Exact prices, booking threshold, appointment duration and cash allocation are not supplied, so feasibility depends on the owner setting them within the limits.

assumptions: Transfer temporarily means reallocating, not increasing, the owner's maximum six additional staff hours.
Pooling the customer relationship means contacting only the forty opted-in customers by existing email.
Pooling capacity means a bounded number of diagnostic appointments whose preparation and delivery fit within six hours.
The owner can offer and price a paid diagnostic service using the existing tools and counter.
The owner defines a paid-booking threshold and stops if it is not reached.
Any pilot cash expenditure, including incidental materials, remains at or below EUR 120 with no recurring commitment.
proposals.proposal: Transfer the owner's available time temporarily into a two-week pilot, pool the forty opted-in customers as the permitted audience, pool the owner's capacity into limited appointments, and diagnose bicycles as a paid pre-service assessment using the existing tools and counter.
proposals.reason: The ordered components can support a distinct paid diagnostic service for existing customers, with limited appointments and no continuing programme. It can satisfy the resource and contact constraints if outreach uses only the existing email channel and delivery uses the existing tools and counter. It is valid only if the temporary time transfer still means no more than six additional staff hours, and if the owner sets a price, any cash spend at or below EUR 120, and a booking or payment threshold. Paid diagnostic bookings provide the demand signal; continue only if the threshold is met, otherwise stop. The proposal does not itself establish those numerical limits, so its feasibility is conditional rather than demonstrated by the seed alone.

assumptions: El silencio momentáneo del mar funciona como huella sensorial aceptable dentro de la premisa especulativa.
proposals.proposal: Cada tarde, oculto el minuto ausente, sigo remendando con mi padre y escucho cómo el mar calla antes de que él lo note.
proposals.reason: Integra ocultamiento, continuidad de la labor y atención al silencio marino en el orden suministrado. El mar que calla hace palpable la ausencia y la diferencia de memoria entre ambos, con tensión clara y sin exposición causal.

assumptions: La expresión «olvida el último» se interpreta como una alusión comprensible al minuto ausente.
proposals.proposal: Cada tarde, oculto el minuto perdido contando los nudos salados de la red mientras mi padre remienda conmigo y olvida el último.
proposals.reason: La acción concreta de contar y ocultar enlaza el trabajo compartido con una textura salada y sugiere el coste emocional de que el padre no recuerde. La secuencia conserva la rutina y cuantifica la ausencia sin explicar su causa.

assumptions: El olor a algas puede funcionar como token de memoria propuesto.
El padre podría notar una alteración en la red o en el tiempo perdido.

components.dimension: A memory token: proposed exploratory concept, not an admitted fact

proposals.proposal: El olor a algas queda en la red; junto a su padre, ella calla el minuto borrado y cose antes de que él note.
proposals.reason: El olor ofrece una huella sensorial memorable y la hija cose para ocultar la ausencia ante su padre. La tensión y el vínculo son claros, aunque 'antes de que él note' vuelve algo explícita la ocultación.

proposals.proposal: Cook and freeze the main batch, portion rice and pasta, portion chickpeas and lentils, and store a tomato-and-seasonal-vegetable component. Schedule Monday chickpeas with rice and vegetables, Tuesday lentils with pasta and vegetables, Wednesday chickpeas with pasta and vegetables, Thursday thawed lentils with rice, and Friday thawed chickpeas with the remaining starch and vegetables.
proposals.reason: This ordered seed directly supports cooking and freezing, portion control, legume-starch variation and a stored vegetable accompaniment. The proposed schedule covers all weekdays and keeps refrigerated cooked food within three days by freezing later portions. It is clear and highly practical, subject to a simple batch being achievable within ninety minutes of active preparation.

assumptions: Rice, pasta, chickpeas and lentils can be batch-cooked within ninety minutes of active preparation.
Some later portions are frozen promptly rather than refrigerated beyond three days.
Seasonal vegetables can be prepared as one adaptable accompaniment.
proposals.proposal: Batch-cook rice and pasta, portion the chickpeas and lentils, and prepare one tomato-and-seasonal-vegetable component to repeat with different portions. Schedule rice with vegetables Monday, lentils with rice Tuesday, pasta with vegetables Wednesday, chickpeas with pasta Thursday, and a frozen or freshly reheated lentil-and-vegetable combination Friday. Freeze portions that will not be eaten within three days.
proposals.reason: The ordered components directly support batch cooking, portioning and varied reuse across five complete weekday meals. The schedule can fit within ninety minutes of active preparation if quantities remain modest, and freezing later portions satisfies the three-day storage rule. Variety is moderate because the same bases and vegetable component recur, while the sequence is clear.

assumptions: A seasonal-vegetable component can be prepared quickly and reused safely across the week.

proposals.proposal: Batch-cook chickpeas and lentils and rice or pasta, portion them, freeze the portions intended for Thursday and Friday, and prepare one quick fresh seasonal-vegetable component for serving Monday through Friday. Schedule Monday chickpeas with rice and vegetables, Tuesday lentils with pasta and vegetables, Wednesday chickpeas with pasta, Thursday thawed lentils with rice, and Friday thawed chickpeas with the remaining grain and vegetables.
proposals.reason: The ordered meanings support portioning the legumes and starches and using the freezer to satisfy the three-day storage limit. The proposed batch and one quick fresh component can fit within ninety minutes of active preparation if the batch is kept simple. The sequence provides five complete meals and meaningful variation through different legume-starch pairings and accompaniments.

assumptions: The selected rice, pasta, chickpea or lentil preparation can be completed within ninety active minutes.
Thursday and Friday portions are frozen promptly and safely reheated.
Different combinations of the same protein, energy and fresh component provide acceptable variety.
proposals.proposal: Thermally transform an energy base such as rice or pasta during the batch cook, distribute a chickpea or lentil protein base across five portions, and reuse a quick fresh vegetable component with different combinations. Eat refrigerated portions Monday through Wednesday and freeze the remaining portions for Thursday and Friday.
proposals.reason: This ordered proposal directly supports a practical five-evening plan: batch cooking supplies the energy and protein, while the reused fresh component creates weekday variation. The refrigeration and freezing schedule satisfies the three-day storage limit, and the plan is clear enough to execute within the stated preparation ceiling if the batch quantities remain modest.

assumptions: Protein and energy bases can be batch-cooked within ninety active minutes.
Chickpeas or lentils provide the planned protein base.
The available seasonal vegetables can serve as the quick fresh component.
proposals.proposal: Distribute the protein base across five portions, allocate the preparation capacity between batch cooking and one quick fresh component, distribute energy bases such as rice and pasta across the weekdays, and combine them with tomatoes and seasonal vegetables. Refrigerate Monday through Wednesday meals and freeze Thursday and Friday meals, using different combinations to create variety.
proposals.reason: The ordered sequence gives the strongest complete structure: protein coverage, bounded preparation, varied energy bases, and final meal assembly. It can satisfy coverage, time and storage constraints, though distributing both protein and energy bases may require more cooking and portion management than the ninety-minute limit allows unless the bases are batch-cooked efficiently.

assumptions: The batch can be portioned into five complete evening meals.
Frozen portions can be thawed in time for Thursday and Friday.
Different available accompaniments are sufficient to create meaningful variety.
proposals.proposal: Partition the ninety-minute preparation capacity into one batch-cooking session and a small fresh-component session, then concentrate the deferred availability into clearly portioned meals: refrigerate portions for the first three days and freeze the remainder for Thursday and Friday. Reuse the base with different rice, pasta, tomato or vegetable accompaniments.
proposals.reason: The ordered sequence directly manages preparation capacity and delayed use, yielding a practical five-evening schedule with storage compliance and moderate variety. It is less explicit about the actual weekday order and relies on proposed portioning and accompaniments to make the meals complete.

assumptions: La hija es el sujeto implícito de “recuerda” y “cambia”.
El goteo persistente de sal se acepta como huella sensorial del minuto.
proposals.proposal: Recuerda el minuto perdido mientras cambia con su padre la red que aún gotea sal.
proposals.reason: La secuencia remember-exchange se convierte en una acción concreta compartida con el padre; el goteo de sal hace palpable la anomalía y sugiere un coste emocional sin explicarla.

assumptions: Cortar la concha es un gesto exploratorio deliberado, no un hecho establecido.
El padre no notar el silencio expresa la asimetría de memoria entre ambos.

components.dimension: A shell: proposed exploratory object, not an admitted fact

proposals.proposal: Al anochecer, ella escucha el minuto ausente mientras corta una concha y su padre corta la red, sin notar el silencio salado.
proposals.reason: La frase es rítmica y sensorial: el silencio salado hace tangible la ausencia y la indiferencia del padre aporta una herida emocional. Las dos acciones de cortar son concretas, aunque cortar una concha resulta algo extraño y la reparación de redes se vuelve una ruptura.

assumptions: «Cortarse la tarde» evocará el minuto perdido sin necesidad de nombrarlo.
Cortar el nudo puede leerse como una amenaza al trabajo común.

components.dimension: A shell: proposed exploratory object, not an admitted fact

proposals.proposal: Ella oculta la concha que rechaza mientras su padre se esconde y, al cortarse la tarde, corta el nudo de la red.
proposals.reason: La secuencia respeta ocultar, rechazar, esconder y cortar. Cortar el nudo es una acción concreta con posible coste para el trabajo compartido, y «cortarse la tarde» sugiere la desaparición sin explicarla; la relación padre-hija queda más implícita.
